decisions.reason: As a relatively peripheral consumer product with less strategic centrality than the firm's industrial waste-to-value technologies, it is easier for management to discontinue it and redirect resources despite some prior investment.
Because it extends the firm's established modular waste-to-energy offering and likely reuses existing engineering capabilities, sunk costs and business fit favor continuing it on the market.
As a publicly presented flagship with clear strategic importance, management is likely to escalate commitment and interpret any weak results as temporary rather than withdraw it.
Its role as a flagship-adjacent waste-to-fuel technology close to the core business makes the firm likely to persist, supported by prior investment and visible commitment.
